outcome: compliance with guidelines for elective Cesarean section
population attributable fractions (PAFs) for shoulder dystocia
cohort: Pregnant women with and without DIP, stratified by Aboriginal status
finding: Aboriginal mothers with DIP had a higher risk of shoulder dystocia, a stronger association between birthweight and shoulder dystocia, and lower rates of guideline-recommended elective Cesarean section, suggesting disparities in care and outcomes.
mod_finding: Aboriginal mothers with DIP had a higher risk of shoulder dystocia and lower rates of guideline-recommended elective Cesarean section.
